transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… my mind doesn’t seem to hold onto things the way it used to. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the numbers and words just sort of scatter on me.
When did you first notice that your mind wasn't holding onto things the way it used to?
About three weeks ago. It was… right after my older sister died.
Are you having trouble remembering things that happened before your sister died?

I don’t know that it’s old memories, exactly. It’s more… lately, when I try to do something simple, like write a note for the youth maker program, the words and numbers just won’t stay put in my head. They scatter.
Do you find yourself having trouble focusing on tasks or activities since your sister died?

Yes… I suppose so. It’s like I said—when I sit down to do even a simple note for the youth maker program, the words and numbers won’t stay in place. They just… scatter, and I can’t keep hold of the task.
Have you been feeling sad or empty since your sister died?
Yes. Most days I wake up with this… heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Even when my wife’s being kind, it still feels like I’m far away somehow… like I’m sitting at the bottom of a well.
Do you find that your thoughts are disjointed or don't make sense to you or others?
I… don’t think so. I lose track sometimes, but I’m not aware of my thoughts not making sense to other people.
Do you have trouble expressing your thoughts in a way that makes sense to others?
Not that I’ve noticed. I mean… I don’t say much lately, but I think when I do, people understand me well enough.
Do you find yourself having difficulty organizing your thoughts when trying to express them?

Yes… I think so. That’s part of why I came in. My mind just doesn’t seem to hold onto things anymore. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the words, the numbers… they just scatter on me.
Do you ever feel confused about where you are or what's happening around you?
No… not really. I mean, I get foggy sometimes, but I know where I am. I don’t think I get confused like that.
Do you ever feel unsure about what day or time it is?
Not usually, no. I might lose track a bit if I’m just sitting around, but I know what day it is if I think about it.
Do you find yourself jumping from one idea to another without finishing your thoughts?

Not jumping exactly… it’s more that I can’t keep hold of the thought. I sit down to write something simple for the youth maker program, and the words or numbers just sort of scatter before I can get it finished.
Do you think your thoughts are well-organized when you're trying to convey them to someone else?

Not as well as I used to. I mean… I can start to explain something, even just a simple note for the youth maker program, and then the words don’t stay lined up. The numbers, too. They kind of scatter on me before I can get it out.
Do you think your mind is playing tricks on you or that your thoughts are not your own?
No… I don’t think so. My thoughts feel like mine. They’re just… harder to keep straight sometimes.
Do you ever feel unsure about who you are?
I don’t think so. I mean… I know who I am. I just don’t always feel much like myself lately.
Do you ever feel disoriented or unsure about your surroundings?
No… I don’t think so. I know where I am. I just… maybe get a little foggy, but not lost or anything.
Are you having difficulty completing everyday tasks because of your memory and concentration problems?

Yes… yeah, it’s been getting in the way. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the words or numbers just… scatter. I can’t hold onto them long enough.
Are these memory and concentration problems causing you significant distress or interfering with your daily life?

Yes. More than I like to admit. I’ve let things slip… church responsibilities, the garden, the youth maker program. My wife and our pastor have had to step in some. And I don’t really feel safe being alone in the workshop anymore.
Do you think your memory and concentration problems started after your sister's death or were they present before, but maybe not as noticeable?
I think it really started after my sister died… about three weeks ago. I may have had little lapses before, but nothing I paid much attention to.
Have you noticed any fluctuations in your symptoms throughout the day?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a clear pattern. It feels… kind of bad most of the time. I haven’t really been tracking whether it changes during the day.
Do you feel like you're fully awake and alert most of the time?
I think so… I mean, I don’t feel like I’m drifting off or anything. I’m just not sure I’d call myself fully sharp most of the time.
